contribution: Participants describe faster exploration and generation, continuing correction needs, more planning/review and expanding workload.
account_basis: Reported current/past work and professional interpretation
qualification: This directly answers changes and continuities in work; speed and workload claims remain self-assessed rather than measured outcomes.

contribution: Participants envisage less administrative effort, more stakeholder attention and additional projects or improvement ambitions.
account_basis: Expected future developments
qualification: These are anticipated directions and conditions, not realized future outcomes.

contribution: Knowledge is recovered and shared, and intent becomes more explicit for agents, while core design rules and the need for context continue.
account_basis: Direct practices, professional interpretations and a colleague report
qualification: Knowledge access and codification attempts are described; reliable agent enforcement or a universal change in artifacts is not established.

contribution: Participants envisage agent-consumable knowledge and testable intent; representation and validated explanation are conditions that could alter human involvement.
account_basis: Desired/expected developments and conditional possibilities
qualification: Desired knowledge tools complement, rather than establish, expected role change; representations and explanations are not assumed complete or reliable.

contribution: Participants attribute a specific contribution to supplying architectural context and meaningful solution boundaries for agents.
account_basis: Conditional value argument and reported colleague concerns
qualification: This supports one mechanism of architectural contribution. Broader domain judgment, trade-offs and risk stewardship are central to T07; knowledge access alone is not proof of professional value.

contribution: Participants describe continued human checking, architectural review and acceptance alongside delegated execution.
account_basis: Personal/organizational practices and a professional interpretation of testing continuity
qualification: This is the work-continuity aspect of an allocation theme; it does not establish unchanged architectural work in general or universal human-only verification.

contribution: Participants distinguish delegated execution from retained human acceptance, decision control and answerability, with different role-holders and responsibility tensions.
account_basis: Own and organizational accounts, a colleague report, professional interpretations and a conditional responsibility argument
qualification: Review, authority and accountability are separate properties. These are situated perceived allocations, not verified legal duties or evidence that architects alone remain responsible.

contribution: Participants discuss difficulty taking responsibility for delegated work, desire retained sign-off and envisage validated explanations as a condition changing human involvement.
account_basis: Conditional scenarios and a normative desire
qualification: A wish to retain sign-off is not a prediction; conditional explanation-based changes are not achieved capability. This is a specific future condition, not a comprehensive role trajectory.

contribution: Some accounts describe wider engineer ownership of architectural tasks; others describe already-shared architecture and no observed reallocation.
account_basis: Reported task arrangements and organizational interpretation
qualification: I8 lacks a reliable pre-adoption company comparison. Changes and continuities in work are retained without attributing every shared arrangement to GenAI.

contribution: Participants describe varied effects on professional boundaries, apparent influence, communication and relationships, including accounts of no authority or boundary change.
account_basis: Reported interactions, own/organizational accounts and role interpretations
qualification: Apparent competence, communication, work ownership and formal decision authority are different properties; no uniform disappearance or authority redistribution is inferred.

contribution: Participants envisage convergence, different role titles or continued specialization, shaped by product complexity and established organizational/team arrangements.
account_basis: Conditional scenarios, contextual interpretation and expected developments
qualification: These are divergent possible trajectories, not verified employment trends or inevitable loss of the architect role.

contribution: Participants report AI policy work, shared feedback and work decomposition, while interpreting the delivery process itself as an architectural concern.
account_basis: Direct personal/organizational work and architectural interpretation
qualification: Current mechanisms are distinguished from prospective orchestration; this does not imply governance or coordination was absent before GenAI.

contribution: Participants perceive responsibilities around permissible AI use, cost stewardship and commercial expectations for AI-supported professional work.
account_basis: Reported permissions, client questions and own policy work, plus professional interpretation
qualification: Client approval and remuneration questions are not evidence of changed legal authority, actual fee changes or measured cost savings.

contribution: Participants expect more upstream process design and envisage staged/coordinated agent work, qualified by shared execution needs, organizational readiness and the limits of excessive constraint.
account_basis: Expected/conditional developments, desired collaboration and reported contextual constraints
qualification: Desired shared execution is not itself a forecast; current organizational immaturity and constraint trade-offs delimit envisaged role evolution.

contribution: Participants expect broader expertise demands and see continued skill formation, trustworthy assistance and opportunities to learn through review as shaping future human participation.
account_basis: Expected proficiency/skill needs and normative or desired learning pathways
qualification: Desired learning and agency conditions are distinguished from predicted outcomes; loss-only trajectories are qualified by positive learning and enjoyment cases.

contribution: Participants value critical understanding, creativity and meaningful human participation that work and learning arrangements can sustain.
account_basis: Value interpretations and reported effort to understand AI output
qualification: This supports capacities and participation valued alongside architectural judgment. Enjoyment or learning alone does not establish the architect’s comparative contribution; T07 carries the central attributed-value claim.

contribution: Participants describe continuing stakeholder purpose and business interpretation, while some interpret cheaper technical reversal as changing which risks deserve architectural attention.
account_basis: Explicit continuity account and professional interpretations of continuity and changing significance
qualification: Actual, interpreted and desired continuity remain distinct. Perceived reversibility is not measured and is not assumed to apply to all technical decisions.

contribution: Participants attribute architectural value to domain and business understanding, stakeholder trade-offs, identifying significant risks and contextual ethical reasoning.
account_basis: Situated value interpretations and an explicit continuity account
qualification: Attributed value is not proof of increased formal authority, permanent AI incapability or measured superiority. The accountability allocation is analyzed separately in T03.

contribution: Different adoption experiences and appraised usefulness help explain variation in described work changes and continuities.
account_basis: Retrospective adoption and usefulness accounts
qualification: These are participant appraisals, not a verified model-development timeline or a universal adoption-stage model.

contribution: Uncertain capability, changing usefulness and representation/explanation conditions qualify all future role trajectories.
account_basis: Future uncertainty and conditional scenarios
qualification: No single expected trajectory is imposed on the differing accounts.

contribution: Participants attribute value to architecture expertise when combining nondeterministic AI features with deterministic systems.
account_basis: Conditional attributed value, a scope qualification and a future complexity account
qualification: Retain the qualification that strategic architectural value may continue rather than universally increase. Theme P01 remains peripheral pending scope review.

contribution: Participants envisage security, identity and assurance complexity when AI is embedded in a delivered system.
account_basis: Expected product-architecture development
qualification: This is not evidence of deployed future capability or a central delivery-process role trajectory.
